title: Close-packed corallites of varying size are on average hexagonal

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Close-packed corallites of varying size are on average hexagonal

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In colonial corals whose corallites are in close contact, the corallites are squeezed into hexagonal prisms; where their sizes vary irregularly they are hexagonal on average, some having fewer and some more than six sides, while loosely bundled corallites stay cylindrical.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: where there is greater and more irregular variation in size, the cells will be _on the average_ hexagonal, but some will have fewer and some more sides than six

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Hexagonal corallites”. Scope: massive versus fasciculate colonial corals (e.g. Lithostrotion, Cyathophyllum, Arachnophyllum)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-10: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Contact state, circularity, and number of sides are directly measurable in existing specimen scans. Public collections are sufficient for a strong test of the main massive-versus-fasciculate and mean-six predictions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Segment colonial coral scans and compare sidedness and circularity between massive close-contact and fasciculate colonies, testing whether mean sidedness is six despite size variation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil deformation can alter sidedness.

Some named historical genera have limited digital coverage.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.88
analysis feasibility: 0.82
operationalizability: 0.96

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Mean side number under close contact, versus cylindrical outlines when corallites are free, is a direct count on public specimen images and scans. Colony growth form is already tabulated and sorts the two habits. Counting a broad sample is weeks of ordinary morphometry, enough to resolve the packing claim for massive versus fasciculate colonies.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count corallite sides in massive colonies whose polyps are in contact and compare the mean and the spread with fasciculate colonies whose corallites stay free. Close-packed colonies with a mean near six sides, more spread where sizes vary, and cylindrical corallites where contact is loose, would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Paleozoic genera named by Thompson are photographed less evenly than living massive corals, and abrasion can round corners.

Side number is not a column in the trait database and has to be counted from images and scans.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.7
data existence: 0.65
operationalizability: 0.9
analysis feasibility: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.55

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If close-packed cells of varying size are on average hexagonal, the mean number of neighbours of fully surrounded cells is 6.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: Cells in each image were segmented with Cellpose CPSAM v2 on the Nebius Scientific AI Platform (claim-sources/cell-geometry/segment.py; operation IDs and model checksum in claim-sources/cell-geometry/results/<image>/cellpose.json). claim-sources/cell-geometry/analyze.py closes inter-cell gaps, finds points where three or more cells meet, estimates each wall's direction from wall pixels 0.08-0.25 median cell diameters from the junction, counts neighbours of cells fully surrounded by segmented cells, and runs the same measurement on three synthetic tilings (hexagonal lattice, brick wall, random Voronoi) as calibration.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Exploratory, not pre-registered: the images were segmented and inspected before the pass criterion was written. Treat the verdict as hypothesis-generating; a pre-registered replication on new images is needed before it counts as a test. A tissue conforms if its mean neighbour number is within 0.1 of 6. Supports if most usable tissues conform.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Refutes if most usable tissues have a mean neighbour number more than 0.1 from 6.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: usable tissues with mean neighbour number within 0.1 of 6

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's example is coral corallites; this tests the same statement on plant and animal cell sheets. Euler's formula forces a mean of 6 for any large planar tiling with three cells at every vertex, so agreement confirms the claim without testing a biological mechanism.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
Morphology of human corneal endothelium in situ.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

Drosophila eye 1000x - SEM MUSE.tif (Wikimedia Commons)

Physcomitrella patens (a, 144649-481016) 6961.JPG (Wikimedia Commons)

Epidermis of Festuca arundinacea.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

Aloe vera Cells, 150X.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Exploratory, not pre-registered: the images were segmented and inspected before the pass criterion was written. Treat the verdict as hypothesis-generating; a pre-registered replication on new images is needed before it counts as a test.

A mean of 6 is a topological necessity for trivalent planar tilings (Euler), reproduced by the random-Voronoi control; it is not evidence for any biological mechanism.

Grass epidermis falls short of 6, most likely because unsegmented stomata and hairs hide some neighbours.

Corallites, Thompson's own example, were not tested.
